Satisfied with this arrangement, the Energy Cooperation Group would release its assets to the management of the National Wealth Fund. At the same time, the ECG Central Commission would vote to voluntarily dissolve itself to make provision for the ECG's reformation into a new entity: The Tartakum Energy Corporation, to operate under the trade name Tencor. A Board of Directors would be reconstituted for the new regime, 50% Tarta, 25% Qianxun, 25% Elseyro-Vespurian. The ECG's new stock name, TTEC, would appear on the Rolena Stock Exchange to account for this fresh rebrand.

With Tartakum's latest oil and gas corporation now set to begin operations on its own, Qianxun would move to finalize the terms of their alliance agreement with Tartakum, with Qianxun diplomats at Tartakum's temporary embassy mulling over details of their arrangement. After brief discussions between these diplomats and members of the Qianxun Central State Commission, and a supplementary consultation with Qianxun business leaders, it was agreed that Tartakum's offer was sound, and later in the day on 28 November 2025, Qianxun would finalize the terms of their military alliance.

New corporations would spring up in Tarta territory overnight. Almstedt Corporation, Dearborn Bank, but also Qianxun industry leaders like Qunarco, Miwu Group, Zhaoxin Technologies JCG, and Canglu JCG, with many rushing to Bazhrut to set up offices and begin production of resources to feed Tartakum's growing economy. At the same time, the Tarta bordas would appreciate to account for this sudden burst of growth.

However, Qianxun advisors would warn Tarta to prepare for the great shift that was to come. With these new companies flooding into the country, and with Qianxun technology influencing the Tarta agricultural sector to release workers to account for increased productivity, there will be a great movement of workers seeking to find new employment in Rolena and Bazhrut. When that happens, the state must ensure for its people the socialist principle of the right to labor, or else risk the discontent of the many to the detriment of the few.

Elsewhere, SummitONE Solutions would also set up their own offices in Tartakum, but would advertise themselves as a "private security company" only empowered to supply armored cars for banks and security guards for private establishments, with the corporation deliberating hiding their military capabilities to avoid risks of public scrutiny, with their technological sector collaborating with Qunarco Group to ensure absolute secrecy.[/quote]

The Tartees Ministry of Relations would be very much pleased at the Alliance being settled, and true partnership starting form. Tarta will be sub-secretly sending Gendarmerie and Para-Military to SummitONE at Qianxuns notice to help out in International Causes. The Tartees Ministry of Labor ensures Qianxun that it will be prepared to let the people work. Also, the Ministry of Defence has said that it will be purchasing over 50 ZTZ-65 to outfit the Gendarmerie and the armies mobile units.  It will also be purchasing the ZSL-18 and the ZTZ-18 for its armored units, with budgeting from Qianxun advisors. Tarta will also be requesting technology and off market weaponry that it could purchase from Qianxun. A recent information leaked to the public by a Insider said "The MOD is starting to purchase Cruise missile and sub-sonic weaponry into it's arsenal".

[spoiler= Expansion Post: Donars Fury (1100 Words)] The first bomb detonated at 5 AM in the city of Hornthal, ripping apart the local rail station. Commuters on their way to the arms factories never made it home. Within an hour, coordinated attacks struck Basilisk and Hochwacht: a car bomb outside the royal ministries, a marketplace massacre, and a gun battle near the parliament square. By the end of the day, nearly 400 Cessenians were dead. The attackers called themselves the Free Donar Army (FDA), a hardline nationalist-separatist group with roots in the eastern highlands. They denounced King Frederic Arminius III as a puppet monarch, demanded the establishment of a Mountain Republic, and had quietly armed themselves for years. What began as sporadic raids in the valleys had escalated into urban terrorism and soon after an open rebellion. The Cessenian Royal Guard fought bravely but was soon overwhelmed. In the time of two weeks, whole valleys fell to insurgent control. Basilisk was under siege. The King broadcast from a fortified palace, appealing to Elseyr:
If the mountains fall to terror, the heart of our continent is lost. We cannot stand alone. The Elseyran Defense Union convened an emergency summit in Heiðabýr, the capital of Jomsland. Jomsland committed 25.000 troops, spearheaded by its famed Úlfhéðnar  and Jomsviking Order. EDU allies dispatched several mountain warfare legions, intelligence units, and humanitarian aid. The mountains awaited them.
General Eirik Hallvarðsson, commander of Jomslands 25.000 troops, landed in Basilisk under cover of night. The city was dark, the power grid destroyed by the insurgents. Smoke drifted from burned-out vehicles. The Royal Guard, bloodied but unbroken, greeted them with weary relief. Their commander, General Gōdrick fon Īstarburg, briefed Hallvarðsson:
They hold the outer passes. We control the palace and a few central districts. Civilians are trapped. Every day the FDA grows bolder.
Jomslands Soldiers went to work. In the old, narrow streets of Basilisk, they fought block by block, clearing insurgent sniper nests and mines. EDU drones provided overwatch, while Cessenian locals guided troops through alleyways.
By the third week, Basilisks siege was broken. Relief convoys rolled in. King Frederic addressed his people again, flanked by EDU officers:
The mountains are scarred, but our spirit is unbroken. With Elseyrs brothers beside us, we will endure. 
Yet the FDA was far from defeated. In the industrial hub of Hochwacht, the insurgents had entrenched themselves in factories and mines, turning steel factories into fortresses. The EDU launched a combined offensive. Jomslandic fighter jets attacked enemy positions, while EDU brigades advanced through the valley. The fighting was brutal. the cities alleyways became battlegrounds, and factory floors echoed with gunfire. Captain Søren Dragosson, a Jomslandic platoon leader, recalled:
It was hell. They fought like demons in the dark, but we were relentless. We carried the dragon banner into every hall until nothing stood.
The victory came at a high cost, nearly 200 EDU casualties. But the FDAs backbone was broken. Surviving Rebels fled deeper into the hills. The war changed from open battles to guerrilla warfare. The FDA used the hilly terrain to their advantage, ambushing convoys and retreating into the forests. To counter this, Jomsland deployed its Fjallgöngumaður troops, specialists in mountain and forest warfare. These warriors, trained in the snowy mountains of thule, moved with deadly efficiency. They hunted FDA Members in the valleys, striking camps at dawn, vanishing before reinforcements arrived. The EDU also started non-military operations. Humanitarian teams rebuilt roads, reopened schools, and distributed food. Refugees who once feared EDU troops began to see them as protectors. But the insurgents wouldnt let this slide. They targeted aid convoys, executed village elders, and broadcast propaganda declaring the EDU occupiers.But just as stability seemed within reach, disaster struck again. A truck bomb detonated outside Basilisks central hospital, killing 30 civilians and 5 EDU medics.
The attack shocked Elseyr. Protests rose up in EDU capitals, some demanding withdrawal, others calling for escalation.In Jomsland, High King Jorik stood before the Althing:
Every drop of Jomslandic blood spilled in Cessenia binds us tighter to her people. We will not retreat. We will crush this terror so thoroughly that the mountains will remember our wrath for more than a thousand winters.
The Operation intensified. Drone strikes eliminated FDA leaders. EDU cyber teams dismantled their propaganda networks. Cessenian intelligence, once fractured, was rebuilt with Jomslandic advisors. Slowly, the FDAs grip weakened. The final campaign came at the foot of Mount Dēvelsberg. Intelligence revealed that the FDA high command had retreated to caves beneath the sacred peak. The assault was a joint operation: Jomslandic Fjallgöngumaður, Cessenian Royal Guard, EDU Mountain Brigades. Under cover of night, they stormed the caves. Fighting raged for two days underground, flashbangs, close-quarters combat, flamethrowers in narrow tunnels.
By the end, the FDA was annihilated. Its leader, Erīch Weißmānn, was captured alive, paraded through Basilisk, and put on trial for crimes against humanity.
The war was over. Though victory had been secured, the Cessenians knew survival alone was not enough. The Free Donar Army had nearly torn their nation apart and without Jomsland and the EDU, the monarchy might not have endured. In the grand halls of Basilisks restored parliament, King Frederic Arminius III addressed his nobles and ministers:
The Free Donar Army has fallen, but the world beyond our mountains grows ever more dangerous. Alone, we are vulnerable. United with our northern brothers, we are guaranteed to survive. I propose that Cessenia take its rightful place within the Second Commonwealth of Jomsland.
The chamber erupted in debate. Some feared a loss of sovereignty, others saw this as a begin of a new era. But the voices of the war-weary people like villagers, miners, farmers, spoke loudest. They remembered the Jomslandic soldiers who had bled in Basilisk, the EDU convoys that brought food and medicine. When the Althing of Jomsland convened in Heiðabýr a few days later later, the High King received the cessenian delegation. The ceremony was held in Bondahall. Before the dragon banner of Jomsland, King Frederic knelt and placed his sword upon the stone floor.
By the blood shed in our mountains, I pledge Cessenia to the Commonwealth. May our people stand as brothers, bound in strength and honor.
High King Jorik III lifted him up, clasping his hand.
From this day forth, you are no longer alone in the mountains. You are one of us, a realm of the Commonwealth. Let the people of Cessenia rise as proud guardians of our northern dominion.
In time, Basilisk became the southern gate of the Commonwealth. Cessenian legions marched beneath the dragon banner, EDU headquarters established a permanent presence in the city, and the Kingdoms famed metalworks supplied stores across the Commonwealth.[/spoiler]

[spoiler=Expansion: the frozen lands (and Bobian land purchase) ~1900 words]
[b]Old tales[/b]
Since ancient times, dating back to the era of the kingdom of Hydronia, people have been aware of the existence of the mysterious arctic continent. For centuries, the arctic was perceived not merely as a harsh, frozen wasteland but as a divine and mystical landscape shaped and carved by the gods themselves. Early Hydronian inhabitants regarded this icy wilderness with reverence, believing it to be a realm imbued with spiritual significance and cosmic power. The icy expanse was seen as a sacred domain, a place where the divine and mortal worlds intersected, and where the forces of nature manifested in awe-inspiring phenomena. As such, it played a central role in the mythologies and cultural narratives of ancient Hydronia, inspiring stories, legends, and rituals that sought to explain its mysterious nature.

Within early Hydronian culture, numerous myths and legends grew around the arctic region, often depicting it as a realm of wonder and enchantment. One of the most well-known tales is the story of the north road, a legendary icy pathway that appears once each year, offering a fleeting gateway to the frozen lands. According to this legend, during the coldest months when the North Sea freezes over, a natural ice corridor forms, creating a temporary bridge across the water. This ice road is believed to be a magical pathway, accessible only during specific celestial alignments or under particular auspices. Travelers who brave the perilous journey along this icy trail are said to reach the distant and enchanted frozen lands, where wondrous snow beings and magical creatures dwell. These beings are described as luminous entities made of pure snow and ice, possessing otherworldly powers and a mysterious beauty that captivates all who encounter them.

The story of the north road also speaks of white beasts that wander along the ice and within the frozen lands. These creatures are now recognized as polar bears, but in early times, they were regarded as mystical or supernatural beings. The ancient Hydronians believed that these polar bears had originally arrived in Hydronia via the north road, which explained their initial unfamiliarity and the sense of awe surrounding them. The polar bears, in the cultural imagination, symbolized strength, endurance, and the divine guardianship of the icy wilderness. The myth persisted that these creatures were not merely animals but were imbued with spiritual significance, serving as messengers or protectors of the sacred arctic realm. Their presence reinforced the idea that the arctic was a realm governed by divine forces, a place that commanded respect and reverence from mortals.

[b]Imperial Exploration[/b]
The Holy Hydronic Empire, which endured from 1310 until its dissolution in 1822, undertook numerous expeditions into the northern reaches of the continent. The earliest recorded attempt to explore the arctic occurred in 1520, shortly after Hydronia had suffered a significant defeat in a war against the kingdom of Sakara, located in the southern regions of the continent. Following this military setback, the emperor shifted strategic focus toward the northern territories, seeking new opportunities, resources, and territorial expansion. In the years immediately preceding this attempt, Hydronia had successfully expanded into parts of northern east Shamat, establishing a series of fortified outposts and trading posts that served as a strategic staging ground for future arctic explorations.

However, the initial expedition faced formidable challenges. The technology available at the time was rudimentary, particularly lacking in high-speed watercraft capable of navigating the icy waters of the North Sea and the Arctic Ocean. The ships used in the expedition were primarily wooden sailing vessels, ill-equipped to handle the treacherous icy conditions. During the winter months, these vessels encountered numerous difficulties, including colliding with large icebergs and being trapped in pack ice. Several ships were crushed or sank after being caught in the unpredictable and often violent ice flows, leading to significant losses and setbacks for the expedition. These early efforts underscored the formidable nature of the Arctic environment and the technological limitations of the era, which hindered the progress of exploration.

It would take another two centuries before the Holy Hydronic Empire attempted to explore the arctic once again. In 1732, a new expedition was commissioned by the emperor, involving five ships equipped with improved technology, including sturdier hulls, better navigational instruments, and provisions designed to withstand prolonged periods in the icy wilderness. Despite these advancements, the undertaking remained perilous. The expedition underestimated some of the logistical challenges involved in arctic exploration. They supplied only limited amounts of food and supplies for the crew, assuming that the expedition would be brief and straightforward. Unfortunately, the supplies ran out within days, leading to widespread starvation among the crew members. Several ships had to abandon their efforts and retreat due to the severity of the conditions and the lack of provisions.

Meanwhile, two of the ships managed to ration their supplies carefully and continued their journey into the arctic. These ships established two separate outposts along the northern coast of the continent, serving as early footholds in the uncharted territory. These outposts represented the first human efforts to establish a presence in the arctic lands, but they soon faced their own difficulties. The outposts lacked sufficient supplies, and harsh environmental conditions made it impossible to sustain them long-term. As a result, both outposts were ultimately abandoned when their resources were exhausted, and the crews retreated southward. These early expeditions, despite their failures, laid the groundwork for future exploration efforts and highlighted the immense challenges posed by the arctic environment.

By the year 1822, all human presence in the arctic territories had been abandoned. The outposts were left deserted, and no permanent settlements or claims remained. Consequently, when the treaty of dissolution was signed, these lands were declared unclaimed and uninhabitedclassified as no mans land. The territories were effectively ignored by the established states of Erene and were not assigned to any nation or jurisdiction. This lack of sovereignty meant that the arctic regions remained outside formal territorial boundaries and were largely considered inaccessible or irrelevant for political or economic purposes at the time. The vast, icy wilderness was regarded as a remote and inhospitable frontier, a place of legend rather than a region of strategic importance.

[b]The Chilly Race[/b]
Fast forward to the mid-20th century, specifically the 1950s and 1960s, when global powers recognized the strategic and military potential of nuclear technology. During this period, nations sought to develop and test nuclear weapons, viewing the remote and harsh environment of the arctic as an ideal testing ground due to its isolation and natural defenses. The Arctics extreme conditions and vast, uninhabited expanses made it an attractive location for clandestine military experiments and nuclear testing, especially in the context of global tensions.

In 1954, the government of Hydronia, initiated an expedition into the arctic region. Their goal was twofold: to revisit and re-establish a presence in the territories previously explored by the Holy Hydronic Empire centuries earlier and to develop their own strategic advantage in the region. Several ships set sail during the summer months, carrying scientific equipment, supplies, and personnel. These vessels aimed to establish a foothold and create scientific outposts that could serve as bases for future military and research activities. The initial endeavors resulted in the establishment of two research outposts in the arctic within just two years, marking a renewed interest in the region and signaling a shift from exploration to strategic dominance.

Over the following decade, Hydronia rapidly expanded its territorial claims in the arctic, establishing additional outposts and scientific research centers across various strategic locations. This expansion was driven by a desire to secure natural resources, project military power, and gain geopolitical influence in the northern regions. By 1977, THEP launched its nuclear weapons program. The initial plan was to use the vast arctic territories as testing grounds for nuclear devices, taking advantage of the remote and unpopulated environment to carry out low-yield tests without immediate risk to populated areas. The first nuclear test in the arctic occurred in 1981, a low-power device that was carefully monitored and analyzed.

However, the environmental and diplomatic repercussions soon became apparent. Environmental groups, international organizations, and neighboring nations expressed concern over the ecological impact of nuclear testing in the fragile Arctic ecosystem. Following a parliamentary vote, the government of Hydronia decided to prohibit nuclear weapons testing in the arctic altogether, citing environmental preservation and the desire to maintain good diplomatic relations. The decision reflected a growing awareness of the ecological sensitivity of the region and the international pressure to protect the Arctic from environmental degradation caused by nuclear activities.

In 1985, Hydronia took a significant step by officially incorporating its arctic territories into its national jurisdiction. This move was controversial and sparked intense debate among political factions, environmentalists, and indigenous communities. Since the arctic lacked a significant indigenous or civilian populationfew permanent settlements or native communities existedofficially establishing these regions as federal states was deemed impractical. Instead, a new administrative classification was created: unfederated territories. These territories were placed under the authority of specialized committees responsible for managing local affairs, scientific research, and resource development. Nonetheless, overarching control remained with the federal government, which retained authority over security, resource management, and scientific activities.

The arctic territories were divided into three such unfederated territories: Point Sadak, Tutku-Usak Land, and Apaciv. Each had its own administrative committee tasked with local governance, scientific oversight, and resource management. These committees operated under the supervision of the central federal authority, ensuring a coordinated approach to development and security. This administrative structure aimed to balance regional autonomy with national oversight, recognizing the unique challenges and strategic importance of the arctic region.

[b](Bobian Land Purchase)[/b]
Historically, the Holy Hydronic Empire had exerted dominance over the Shamatine Strait, controlling numerous islands and territorial claims on both sides of this vital waterway. Control of key strategic locations, such as the island of Kastakum located at the entrance to the strait, was crucial for maintaining influence over maritime trade routes. However, following the empires decline in 1822, control over these strategic points shifted. The Bobian Empire, a rising power in the world, captured and claimed Kastakum Island during the final war, establishing it as a key military and trading outpost. The islands strategic location made it an important asset for controlling access to the Shamatine Strait and exerting influence over maritime navigation in the area.

By the turn of the 21st century, Hydronia recognized the strategic importance of regaining influence over the strait and its surrounding territories. Diplomatic efforts began to gain momentum, with Hydronian officials seeking to negotiate the purchase of Kastakum Island from the Bobian authorities. The negotiations were driven by a desire to reassert dominance over the maritime region, secure trade routes, and strengthen national security. The relations between Hydronia and the Bobian Republic had improved significantly since the signing of the Treaty of Dissolution, with increased trade, diplomatic exchanges, and mutual interests fostering cooperation.

In February 2000, Hydronia officially initiated diplomatic negotiations with the Bobian authorities, proposing to purchase Kastakum Island for a sum of 5 million Gilders. The negotiations proceeded smoothly, aided by diplomatic channels and mutual understanding of the strategic importance of the island. By November 2001, the deal was finalized, and Hydronia acquired control of Kastakum Island. The island was then incorporated into Hydronian territory as a military district, serving as a strategic outpost for military and economic purposes. Since reasserting control, Hydronian forces have utilized the island to enforce maritime blockades, conduct surveillance, and impose embargoes against the hostile, warmongering states of Erene. This strategic positioning ensures that Hydronia maintains unobstructed trade routes through the strait, reducing reliance on foreign maritime navigation and asserting its influence over the regions geopolitics.
[/spoiler]
